Empirical Research Plan: “The Causal Impact of Unionization Attempts and Certifications on U.S. Private-Sector Establishments, 1984-2001”  

=====================================================================

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
Primary strategy: Local sharp Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the 50 percent certification threshold in NLRB elections.

Why RDD?  
• The NLRB requires a simple majority of votes cast for certification.  
• Among elections decided by very small margins, the outcome is plausibly as-good-as-random because neither side knows the final vote count ex-ante (secret ballot, last-minute campaigning, uncertainty over turnout).  
• Comparing establishments where the union barely won (treated) with those where it barely lost (control) delivers an unbiased estimate of the causal effect of gaining legal bargaining rights, while holding constant the fact that all establishments experienced a union drive.  
• Longitudinal outcomes before and after the election allow dynamic event-study graphs within the RDD window (“difference-in-discontinuities”) to explore anticipation and adjustment paths.

Secondary strategy (anticipatory wage response when the union ultimately loses):  
Difference-in-Differences event study comparing (i) establishments that faced a petition but the union lost (within 5–20 p.p. of the cutoff) with (ii) matched establishments with no petition in the same industry-state-year cell.  This isolates effects of the organizing attempt itself, net of certification.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable (RDD):  
T_i = 1 if the union wins the certification election (union vote share ≥ 0.5), 0 otherwise.

Control group:  
Establishments with union vote share just below 0.5.

Running variable:  
m_i = vote_share_i – 0.5 ; cutoff at m_i = 0.

Bandwidth:  
Main: ±6 percentage points (p.p.) around the cutoff; alternate robustness ±4 and ±8 p.p.

Event/timing:  
Date 0 = election date.  Outcomes observed at t = –3,…,+7 years (balanced where data allow).  Petition date used to test anticipatory effects.

For the DiD anticipatory analysis:  
Treatment = “petition filed but union ultimately loses”; Control = “no petition ever filed”, matched on 4-digit SIC, state, establishment size and pre-petition employment trend.  Event date = petition filing year.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Local random assignment near the 50 percent threshold: establishments cannot precisely manipulate one or two votes.  
Plausibility: High—secret ballot, uncertain turnout, intense but imperfect information.

A2. Continuity of potential outcomes in vote margin at m = 0: absent certification, outcomes would evolve smoothly.  
Plausibility: Reasonable.  We will test for covariate continuity and pre-trend equality.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): one establishment’s certification does not directly affect another’s outcomes within the narrow window.  
Plausibility: High—union bargaining is establishment-specific; geographic spillovers are limited within the tiny RDD bandwidth.

A4. No differential measurement error or attrition precisely at cutoff.  
Plausibility: Possible concern because closure is itself an outcome; we will conduct bounding exercises and report inverse-probability weighted estimates.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
Threat 1: Manipulation of vote counts or turnout in very close elections.  
• McCrary density test of vote margins.  
• Randomization inference comparing predetermined covariates (industry, 3-year pre-trends) across win/loss within bandwidth.

Threat 2: Differential survival (sample attrition) if certification causes exit, removing treated units from later panels.  
• Estimate effect on survival first.  
• Use Lee bounds and IPW re-weighting to adjust for observed attrition.  
• Report balanced-panel estimates plus intent-to-treat on full sample using missing-outcome indicators.

Threat 3: Heterogeneous treatment effects or manipulation of bandwidth choice.  
• Report results across multiple symmetric bandwidths (±4, ±6, ±8 p.p.).  
• Local linear and quadratic specifications; robust bias-corrected confidence intervals (rdrobust).  
• Show that results are smooth when pseudo-cutoffs are placed at ±10 p.p.

5. R CODE OUTLINE (executable)  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
#############################################
# 0. Packages
#############################################
library(data.table)     # fast wrangling
library(fixest)         # high-dim FE / robust se
library(rdrobust)       # RDD implementation
library(ggplot2)

#############################################
# 1. Load & merge data
#############################################
elections  <- fread("nlrb_elections_1984_1999.csv")       # vote tallies etc.
infoUSA    <- fread("infousa_2001.csv")                   # survival/employment/output
lrd        <- fread("lrd_manufacturing_1984_2001.csv")    # annual plant data

# merge by establishment identifier (assumed cleaned)
firmdata   <- merge(elections, infoUSA, by = "estab_id", all.x = TRUE)
firmdata   <- merge(firmdata, lrd,      by = c("estab_id","year"), all.x = TRUE)

#############################################
# 2. Construct variables
#############################################
firmdata[, vote_share := union_yes / (union_yes + union_no)]
firmdata[, margin     := vote_share - 0.5]               # running variable
firmdata[, treat_win  := as.integer(vote_share >= 0.5)]  # sharp RDD

# Create relative year to election for panel specs
firmdata[, rel_year := year - election_year]

# Example outcome: employment (lrd employment if available, else InfoUSA)
firmdata[, lemp := log(employment + 1)]

#############################################
# 3. Main RDD (cross-section, first-differences optional)
#############################################
# Keep closest elections ±6 p.p.
sample_rdd <- firmdata[abs(margin) <= 0.06 & rel_year == 3]  # effect 3 years after

# rdrobust for employment
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = sample_rdd$lemp, x = sample_rdd$margin,
                   c = 0, h = 0.06, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
summary(rd_out)

#############################################
# 4. Dynamic event-study within RDD window
#############################################
dyn <- firmdata[abs(margin) <= 0.06 & rel_year %between% c(-3,7)]

# interact treat_win with rel_year dummies (omit −1 as base)
dyn[, rel_fac := factor(rel_year)]
event_mod <- feols(lemp ~ i(rel_fac, treat_win, ref = -1) |
                   estab_id + year,
                   data = dyn, cluster = ~estab_id)
etable(event_mod)

#############################################
# 5. Anticipatory wage response (DiD)
#############################################
# Flag petition losers
firmdata[, loser := (treat_win == 0)]
# Construct matched control sample externally—assume flag `matched_nopet`
ant_data <- firmdata[past_petition == 1 | matched_nopet == 1]

wage_mod <- feols(log(avg_wage) ~ loser * i(rel_fac, ref = -1) |
                  estab_id + year,
                  cluster = ~estab_id, data = ant_data)
etable(wage_mod)

#############################################
# 6. Robustness: bandwidth 4 p.p.
rd_out4 <- rdrobust(y = sample_rdd$lemp, x = sample_rdd$margin,
                    h = 0.04)
summary(rd_out4)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
Economic priors are ambiguous: unions may raise wages and reduce profitability, potentially lowering survival, yet they can also improve communication and productivity.

• Survival: Small negative effect (−2 to −5 p.p. over 5 years).  
• Employment & output: Slight decline (−3 % to −4 %).  
• Productivity (value added per worker): Likely unchanged or mildly positive (0–2 %).  
• Wages: Increase of 2–4 % in certified plants; in loser plants anticipate a smaller, temporary bump (~1 %) around petition year that fades.

Given 1984-1999’s hostile environment, magnitudes are expected to be modest relative to classic 1970s estimates.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (RDD)  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: Smooth density of running variable at cutoff ………………… 1  
C2: Covariate balance across cutoff within bandwidth ………… 1  
C3: No other policy discontinuities at 50 % …………………………… 1  
C4: Robustness to bandwidth & polynomial choices …………… 1  
C5: External validity beyond close elections ………………………… 0  (local LATE)

Total = 4 / 5.  Local causal effect is internally valid; external validity is limited to close elections.
